body:
P2-12 PLAN 2/6: WHAT EACH SLICE PROVES AND DOES NOT (what each slice is, its size and what a person notices are in the table of the P2-12 section; each merges on its own; "held" = until b11, D2)
Slice 1 (server, M). PROVES: the shapes against recordings, the politeness numbers on a fake clock, B-124 on the new paths ("could not ask" never cached), no ref or row made by a read, the switch opens no socket. DOES NOT PROVE: that a phone uses it, Deezer's real limits, latency. Mergeable before b11 only if the hold is lifted for it (additive, nothing calls it).
Slice 2 (app, M; the phone asks its server). Every screen and every multi-call chain unchanged; DeezerClient stays for a plain server (STOP-GAP, trigger slice 7); 4 s per call; [perf] spans; the P1-16 line when an Encore server lacks the feature. PROVES: every catalogue screen reads through the interface, the new shapes parse (fixtures written by the server's own test), ranking unchanged (the 20 recorded searches). DOES NOT PROVE: a faster artist page (that is slice 3), or the cost of the extra hop (measured in the walk, N7 of docs/19). Held.
Slice 2b (app, S; B-83): a tap on a catalogue list sends ONE POST refs/resolve with every description and queues every ref (the one-at-a-time run stays only for the plain path until P2-20). PROVES: one resolve for 14 songs, nothing half queued after a failed resolve. DOES NOT PROVE: first-song latency on a phone. Held.
Slice 3 (server + app, M; THE N-14 FIX). PROVES: one catalogue request per visit (app test), the identity rule, its basis and its persistence across a restart (server tests), perf spans before and after on VM 108. DOES NOT PROVE: that the first-ever visit of an artist the server never identified is as fast as a warm one (one outside request for the identity, then three in parallel), nor which namesake a person means when nothing proves it. Held.
Slice 4 (design, S, parallel with 1 to 3): the two new lines drawn in all states (docs/design/directions and the inventory), no code; no screen is coded before its drawing exists. Mergeable (docs).
Slice 5 (server + app, M; N-23b; needs P2-25 and slice 4). PROVES: the rule table on both sides, the cap of 2 extra requests, the primary results untouched. DOES NOT PROVE: that every real band is found (15 chosen pairs; an unknown band Deezer does not return stays not found). Held.
Slice 6 (server + app, L; one search on the server): the artist + title reading, the padding filter, namesake ranking and libraryArtistId move into the search within the ceiling of 7; albums/match serves album_gap and the cover fallback; alerts use the Encore client (interim until P2-15); artist_aware_search.dart, ArtistLookupCache and the alerts map are deleted. PROVES: the same Top results on the 20 recorded searches, ceilings counted. DOES NOT PROVE: that the ranking is right (it stays on the phone; "busta" and "metalica" belong to N-16 and P1-07). Held.
Slice 7 (app, S). Delete deezer_client.dart, its two construction sites, the plain-server branch and the ratchet baseline entry. PROVES: the ratchet map no longer lists the file; a counting adapter sees no request to api.deezer.com in a full run of the catalogue screens. After it the sentence is "no call to Deezer's API", NOT "no outside call" (pictures). Held.
Slice 8 (server + app, M). A background identity errand (the artist finder's machinery, at most 20 library artists an hour, background priority) so every library artist is identified without a visit; the phone's name matching of catalogue artists deleted (B-46, with P2-25); B-84's phone half (the library's search for every alphabet: the FTS tokenizer and query pattern, per-character Han, Kana and Thai, harakat; one shared table with P2-25). Held.
Slice 9 is the lead's board work: create the items this plan names, with the triggers above as notes.
Order: 1, then 2 and 4 in parallel, 2b, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8. N-14 wanted sooner: build 1 to 3 as one stack of small PRs, never a phone-side stop-gap.
